items.body: The ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment. Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research. Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance. This week's first stock pick is Datadog , an AI-powered observability and security platform. The company will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption.

items.title: Thousands of jobs at Virgin Media O2 to be cut
items.summary: The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be axed but it will likely be a sizeable chunk of its workforce, the BBC understands.
items.body: Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff face redundancy risk as the telecoms firm looks to save money in the face of billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition. The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be cut but it is likely be a sizeable chunk of its 16,000 workforce, the BBC understands. VMO2 has billions of debt on its balance sheet and is tackling competition from both smaller providers as well as giants like BT, which has agreed a deal to acquire rival TalkTalk, a move which VMO2 has firmly opposed. VMO2 declined to comment. The Prospect union, which represents VMO2 staff, said the cuts were "disappointing and very unsettling".

items.title: Investors pull billions in funds from Binance after record $6.3bn hack
items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange has begun to allow withdrawals after theft believed to have come from North Korea Investors have pulled $3.6bn (£2.7bn) in funds from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance as it recovers from a record hack in which billions were stolen from customer…
items.body: Investors have pulled $3.6bn (£2.7bn) in funds from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance as it recovers from a record hack in which billions were stolen from customer accounts. The platform was hit by a $6.3bn theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history. Experts identified North Korea as the probable culprit . Binance initially froze withdrawals as it investigated the breach but on Sunday announced it had begun a phased reopening . By Sunday afternoon, the platform had processed $4.6bn in withdrawals and $1bn in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of about $3.6bn – representing 2.1% of its $171bn in total assets under management. The numbers were confirmed by the company in its latest proof of reserves snapshot. A full report is expected on Monday.

items.title: Why some EU and Chinese firms are keen to cooperate – even as tensions simmer
items.summary: While trade tensions between Beijing and Brussels remain elevated, some European businesses are pointing to disruptions from the United States as a bigger challenge. Instead, they are seeking closer cooperation with China, even as Chinese carmakers scramble to front-load exports…
items.body: While trade tensions between Beijing and Brussels remain elevated, some European businesses are pointing to disruptions from the United States as a bigger challenge. Instead, they are seeking closer cooperation with China, even as Chinese carmakers scramble to front-load exports ahead of potential future trade barriers. At last week’s 19th Europe-China Business and Technology Cooperation Fair in the southwestern Chinese city of Chengdu, the appetite for closer business ties was evident. Hundreds of Chinese and European companies across a wide range of sectors filled a hall for matchmaking sessions, rotating between tables to exchange ideas and seek potential partners and investors. Some European business representatives said they were not too worried about tensions, instead seeing significant potential for cooperation in sectors such as automotive, renewable energy and agriculture.

items.title: Why AI is boosting Meta's ad business while hurting Google search
items.summary: The gap between Meta's ad revenue growth and Google's search expansion was the widest it's been since 2021 in the latest quarter.
items.body: Google and Facebook have dominated the internet for the past two decades, turning billions of eyeballs into trillions in advertising dollars over that stretch. But with the ChatGPT era altering how consumers engage online, the companies are diverging. In the third quarter , Meta's ad business grew more than twice as quickly as Google's Search and other unit, backing up Mark Zuckerberg's claim that his company's investments in artificial intelligence are leading to better targeting tools for brands to promote goods and services across Facebook and Instagram. Google's problem is that chatbots are becoming an alternative to search, leading consumers to click far fewer blue links and hurting Google's ad revenue. Anthropic's Claude chatbot and Meta's recently launched Muse assistant are adding to the mix.

items.title: The midterm election could reshape the muni bond market. Here’s what investors need to know
items.summary: The 2026 election could affect municipal bonds through state tax measures, new bond supply and the makeup of Congress.
items.body: The outcome of Tuesday's election is expected to have broad implications across the market, including municipal bonds. The spotlight has been on the battle for congressional control and whether Democrats will wrest the House of Representatives, the Senate or both from Republicans. But for the muni market, what happens at the state level could have bigger repercussions — at least in the near term. There is an array of initiatives on ballots around the nation that could change tax laws and add to bond supply. Taxes matter to muni investors since the income received is free of federal tax, as well as state tax if the holder lives in the state where the bond is issued. Depending on the location, ballot measures are up for approval that would either provide tax breaks, or raise taxes on the wealthy.

items.title: No more washing up: How Airbnb's new house rules have divided hosts and guests
items.summary: Airbnb hosts must stop asking guests to wash-up or take out bins under rules coming into force in November.
items.body: When Lisa Clewes returned to her Welsh holiday let after a group of guests checked out, she was horrified by the mess. Just days earlier, she had met the group in person and helped with their luggage. But after a dinner party, the house was left "in a complete mess" with broken glasses, drinks cans on the floor, pans full of food on the table and fish guts left in the garden. "It was really unbelievable. Had I had another booking the same day, I would have had to cancel or delay check-in," says Clewes. She charges a cleaning fee that covers around 75% of the cost of a cleaner and asks guests to empty the fridge, put rubbish in the bins and load the dishwasher. But Airbnb's new rules mean hosts can no longer ask guests to do jobs normally carried out by cleaners, including washing and putting away dishes, stripping beds and taking rubbish off site.

items.title: National Grid to site biggest substation in UK near planned Teesside datacentre
items.summary: New electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for large-scale AI infrastructure National Grid has taken a step towards building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, which could supply power to a vast neighbouring datacentre as…
items.body: National Grid has taken a step towards building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, which could supply power to a vast neighbouring datacentre as the UK races to expand its AI infrastructure. Last week, the company agreed to purchase 29.5 hectares (73 acres) of land at Dorman Point on a site owned by Teesworks, a local private-public partnership. The deal was first reported by Sky News. The deal followed reports last year that the UK government had picked Teesworks as the site for a new artificial intelligence datacentre, and planning applications had been submitted for a project that would span nearly 500,000 sq metres.

items.title: Guangzhou reclaims crown as China’s busiest airport after US$8 billion mega expansion
items.summary: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport has reclaimed its position as China’s busiest airport, handling more than 67 million passenger trips in the first nine months of 2026 following a major expansion last year, the municipal government announced. The airport overtook Shanghai…
items.body: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport has reclaimed its position as China’s busiest airport, handling more than 67 million passenger trips in the first nine months of 2026 following a major expansion last year, the municipal government announced. The airport overtook Shanghai Pudong International Airport, which handled 66.58 million passenger trips during the same period, official data showed. Baiyun had fallen behind Pudong in 2024 and 2025. The expansion took half a decade to complete and includes a new third terminal and fifth runway. It cost 53.77 billion yuan (US$8.1 billion) and broke long-standing bottlenecks by increasing Baiyun’s annual passenger capacity to 120 million, the municipal government said on its official WeChat account. Authorities projected it would handle 90 million passenger trips this year.

items.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
items.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says North Korea was responsible for the hack.
items.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday. The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added. Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday. In an update on Sunday, Binance said withdrawals had been restored on several of its networks, after they were suspended following the hack. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the attack.

items.title: Labour’s pledge to level-up minimum wage for under-20s before next election in doubt
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey fails to guarantee equalisation with adult wage will happen in timeframe set out in manifesto Labour looks less likely to meet its manifesto pledge to equalise the minimum wage for younger workers before the next election, after the chancellor failed to…
items.body: Labour looks less likely to meet its manifesto pledge to equalise the minimum wage for younger workers before the next election, after the chancellor failed to guarantee the rise would happen within that timeframe. John Healey said on Sunday his party was “prepared to take hard decisions about the priorities in government”, including possible spending cuts. His comments came as a former adviser to Andy Burnham, the economist Andy Haldane, warned that UK public finances were in a perilous state and the government was “on a precipice” of a Liz Truss-style meltdown. Government sources expressed anger at the comments, saying the markets had responded positively to the budget. Healey said in interviews on Sunday that he wanted to take the minimum wage increase at a slower pace for younger workers.

items.title: Hormuz woes, climate change boost China’s green energy sales at Canton Fair
items.summary: During the first phase of the ongoing Canton Fair, China’s biggest trade expo, a solar power and energy storage exhibition hall attracted thousands of visitors a day. Chinese manufacturers sought to capitalise on concerns about restricted shipments of oil through the Strait of…
items.body: During the first phase of the ongoing Canton Fair, China’s biggest trade expo, a solar power and energy storage exhibition hall attracted thousands of visitors a day. Chinese manufacturers sought to capitalise on concerns about restricted shipments of oil through the Strait of Hormuz and global climate change trends by turning overseas demand for reliable power into orders. Xu Leiping, deputy general manager of sales at Zhejiang Era Solar Technology, said the company had begun selling a newly developed lightweight solar panel designed for balcony use in July. Each panel covers about 1.5 square metres (16.1 square feet) and weighs roughly 2kg (4.4 pounds), compared with about 14kg (30.9 pounds) for a conventional panel the same size. Xu said the lower weight cut installation and hardware costs by 15 to 20 per cent compared with traditional rooftop mounting systems.

items.summary: Santander, Novartis and other companies say AI is beginning to boost revenue, cut costs or improve profitability as investors seek returns.
items.body: Some companies are beginning to report financial benefits from artificial intelligence investments, as interest in the technology shifts from hype to measurable returns in the latest quarter. Corporate AI investment has surged as companies look to boost efficiency and become more profitable, reaching $581.7 billion in 2025, up 130% from the previous year, according to the Stanford HAI 2026 AI Index report . As CEOs tout the tech's benefits and hyperscalers like Microsoft , Amazon , Google and Meta are expected to spend $700 billion combined this year on its infrastructure, investors are looking for measurable gains. Now, with third-quarter earnings season underway, some companies are beginning to put numbers around those benefits.

items.title: How Rachel Reeves has mapped out the economic agenda for Andy Burnham’s government
items.summary: On Brexit, devolution and investment, the former chancellor is eerily in tune with the man who sacked her Reeves says UK’s future is in the EU Which senior politician has argued that “Brexit did deep damage” and that the government seeks “not to turn back the clock but to look…
items.body: Which senior politician has argued that “Brexit did deep damage” and that the government seeks “not to turn back the clock but to look toward a new and stable, future relationship?” It was not Andy Burnham, who has been the torchbearer for thinking the unthinkable on Brexit since he became prime minister. Instead, these are the words of the former chancellor Rachel Reeves, in a lecture six months ago. Reeves has taken a more thoughtful approach on how to come to terms with life outside government than some of her fellow former ministers. A speech at Harvard on Monday will be her first public intervention on her own record and on Britain’s future, wisely left until after John Healey’s first budget . She will say no one in government could “be in any doubt” about her view on the damage of Brexit – and her belief that one day the UK should return to the EU fold.

items.title: Everything changed for the oil, AI and bond trades over the past month
items.summary: The market expects oil to keep rising, but treasury yields have declined, a warning traders and investors may be more worried about an AI crash than inflation.
items.body: If there was one safe bet over the course of 2026, it was that treasury yields would rise alongside a move up in oil futures contracts. Over the past month, that ended, and according to Jeffrey Rosenberg, senior portfolio manager of the Systematic Alternatives ETF ( IALT ) at BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, the breakdown in that trade has big implications for the market. "Oil and treasury yields had this amazing correlation and in October it just stopped," Rosenberg said on the most recent CNBC "ETF Edge." The relationship between oil and bond yields was featured in Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's FOMC press conference on Wednesday, with Warsh noting how oil futures have continued to rise, a factor the central bank must consider in its fight against inflation.

items.title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
items.summary: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.
items.body: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living. Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who were targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day. They were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service. The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

items.title: Sadiq Khan calls for cap on numbers of robotaxis on London streets
items.summary: Mayor questions impact on air quality, congestion and jobs as government poised to allow driverless vehicles in capital London’s mayor has called for a cap on the numbers of robotaxis on its streets, with the UK government poised to allow fully driverless vehicles to operate in…
items.body: London’s mayor has called for a cap on the numbers of robotaxis on its streets, with the UK government poised to allow fully driverless vehicles to operate in the capital. Sadiq Khan said politicians had failed to “grasp the pace of change” from the technology, which could threaten jobs and increase congestion in the city, and questioned whether the rules for autonomous cars were fit for purpose. His comments came after Chinese robotaxis, now being tested in London, were unveiled by Freenow by Lyft , a rival to Uber. In September Uber started offering limited passenger services in Wayve’s self-driving cars , albeit with a safety driver in the front seat, under licence from Transport for London (TfL). Freenow by Lyft is hoping to launch fully driverless Baidu robotaxis as early as next year, under a national licensing scheme.

items.title: Trump defamation suit against Murdoch, WSJ over Epstein letter dismissed with prejudice
items.summary: President Donald Trump denied writing a birthday letter to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, which was the subject of a 2025 Wall Street Journal article.
items.body: A federal judge in Miami on Saturday dismissed with prejudice President Donald Trump's amended defamation lawsuit against media baron Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal over the newspaper's reporting on a purported 50th birthday letter from the president to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein . District Court Judge Darrin Gayles ruled that Trump had again failed to plausibly allege the newspaper and other defendants acted with actual malice when they published the story in July 2025. "As with his first attempt, he has failed," Gayles wrote in the 20-page ruling , which came more than six months after he dismissed Trump's first version of the suit.

items.title: Energy bills help 'doesn't go far enough'
items.summary: Families in the West Midlands say they are worried about paying winter energy bills.
items.body: Households in the West Midlands said they want to see the government revisit energy bills in the wake of the Budget - amid concerns the help being offered won't go far enough. Chancellor John Healey announced a £100 'household energy payment' , and a future plan to remove gas standing charges, as part of a wider package to address the cost of living. Families in the region told the BBC they were "grateful" for the assistance, but were concerned about their finances over the winter. Kelly Birkett, a personal accountant from Redditch, said: "The £100 is good, but it's not great. It just gets absorbed into everything else families have to pay for, just to get by." Birkett, a married mum-of-two, said her family was already considering what to cut back on in the wake of the Budget. "I know I sound a little but ungrateful for the £100, and I don't want to be.

items.title: A gift to scammers: why you should probably keep your birthday a secret
items.summary: Using a fake DOB or leaving the field blank when making an online account can offer protection from identity theft You get a call from your bank saying there has been suspicious activity on your account. They read out your name, address and date of birth so you are happy it is a…
items.body: You get a call from your bank saying there has been suspicious activity on your account. They read out your name, address and date of birth so you are happy it is a legitimate caller. But you are talking to criminals who have used your date of birth as part of a web of verifying information to convince you they are someone else. People’s DOBs are often held in online accounts after being entered as part of a sign-up process for a retailer, loyalty scheme, newsletter or online competition. In a recent hack of the online retailer Asos customers’ dates of birth were among the details taken by scammers. Now cybersecurity professionals have warned people to resist entering a date of birth, or to put in a fake one, to limit the amount of personal data that is online, frustrating criminals’ attempts to “jigsaw” together personal profiles.

items.title: Diwali hampers to bring hope to families in need
items.summary: The Diwali Basket Brigade volunteers want to help vulnerable households with rising food prices.
items.body: Hundreds of volunteers have packed food parcels to distribute to people across Birmingham struggling with the rising cost of living. About 300 people turned up to the Diwali Basket Brigade event at the RSRS Centre in Hockley, which was organised by The Diwali Foundation. It is the ninth time the charity has brought community volunteers from a variety of backgrounds together to make hampers in the build up to the religious festival. Deepak Parekh, founder of the initiative, said: "[The] cost of living crisis hasn't gone away... but Diwali is a celebration of light over darkness, and this is our little way of bringing some light and some hope into the families that need it most." The Diwali Foundation, who are based in Herefordshire, said that more than 12% of UK households are experiencing food poverty.

items.title: Fashion and tradition: how John Smedley is innovating in a tough market
items.summary: In the final article in a series on high-end British manufacturing we look at a clothing brand that dates to the 18th century but is increasingly on-trend Making jeans again: the Hiut Denim factory in Cardigan Rolls-Royce rides high on craze for customisation Luxury leather:…
items.body: Tina is wielding a large pair of scissors with authority, slicing with immense skill and precision. With 38 years of experience, she is an important member of the 230-strong manufacturing team producing fine knitwear for the John Smedley brand. Using a chalk, a semi-circular guide and a sharp pair of scissors, she cuts necklines in the knitted garments ready for the final trim to be attached. The brand’s site in the Peak District, Derbyshire , is the oldest continuously operating factory in the world, with a maze of buildings, one of which dates to 1784. Inside is a mix of hi-tech Japanese knitting technology, skilled artisans such as Tina, who finish garments by hand, and some machines which date back more than 60 years and have to be kept going with bespoke parts. Another smaller Smedley factory, in Armthorpe, South Yorkshire, also finishes the garments.

items.title: I'm a psychologist who studies couples: People in the happiest relationships do 1 thing differently after time apart—whether it's hours, days or weeks
items.summary: Psychologist Mark Travers argues that the first few minutes after time apart are key to a close, happy relationship, and shares five tips to get them right.
items.body: There's a two-minute window every evening when couples can either strengthen their bond with each other or unknowingly weaken it. In my experience as a psychologist who studies couples, what separates the happy couples from the unhappy ones isn't necessarily how often they argue or how much time they have together. It's whether the two people are genuinely in contact with each other's lives. Partners in happy relationships know what the other one is really going through, week after week. The unhappy ones have often slipped into a kind of parallel coexistence, where they share a home and a calendar and not much else. That difference can be built or lost in moments that may feel too small to matter. I call them "reentry moments." "Reentry moments" are the first minute or two when a couple comes back together after time apart.

items.title: The measure slipped into UK budget that could protect spending on children, youth and rough sleeping | Heather Stewart
items.summary: PDEL, which will ringfence money for preventive policies, marks a welcome and potentially consequential addition John Healey’s debut budget was far from a blockbuster, but it may come to be remembered for the birth of a plucky new character in the tax and spend universe – little…
items.body: John Healey’s debut budget was far from a blockbuster, but it may come to be remembered for the birth of a plucky new character in the tax and spend universe – little PDEL. It may not have the charm of Disney’s Wall-E, but PDEL (pronounced P-Del), or preventative departmental expenditure limit, to give it its full name, marks a welcome, and potentially very consequential, addition. The chancellor made clear that ahead of what the Institute for Fiscal Studies has said will be a “brutal” spending review next year, the Treasury is prepared to ringfence the budget for preventive policies. The impetus for the move came partly from No 10. Andy Burnham knows that to achieve some of the missions closest to his heart, such as tackling rough sleeping , he will have to make the argument that it’s worth spending more upfront to save the state in the longer term.

items.body: Donald Trump ’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines. Fears of new tariffs flare up from time to time when the US president goes off the rails – for instance, threatening to end US trade with countries with which it has a deficit unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. But the sense that the world’s two largest economies are plowing ahead into an overt economic conflagration has taken a back seat to other, more salient fears, about Trump ending American democracy, AI killing us all and stuff like that. The sense of calm is misleading. Under the radar, the world is marching toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that, history suggests, could well spill over into the real thing.

items.summary: Hundreds of adult gaming centres in England have bingo licences that still qualify them for discounted business rates Hundreds of high street “ slot farms ” could continue claiming a discount on their business rates, unless the government closes a loophole that allows them to…
items.body: Hundreds of high street “ slot farms ” could continue claiming a discount on their business rates, unless the government closes a loophole that allows them to pose as bingo halls. John Healey singled out adult gaming centres (AGCs) in his first budget this week, in which he increased duty on slot machine takings from 20% to 25%, claiming he was “raising taxes on gambling to support good growth on every high street”. As well as raising the duty, which will also affect bookmakers and casinos , he said AGCs and vape shops in England would no longer be eligible for a discount on business rates aimed at leisure and hospitality businesses. The prime minister, Andy Burnham, has been a vocal critic of AGCs and posted on Instagram after the budget to back the policy, a key plank of his pitch to improve British high streets.

items.summary: The problems run deep in South Africa’s largest city. Will voters punish the ANC in next week’s local elections? One week before the local elections in South Africa, the pavements and roads of the Johannesburg township Alexandra were filled with piles of rubbish, rotting in the…
items.body: The problems run deep in South Africa’s largest city. Will voters punish the ANC in next week’s local elections? O ne week before the local elections in South Africa , the pavements and roads of the Johannesburg township Alexandra were filled with piles of rubbish, rotting in the heat. At the Jukskei River, its banks choked with rubble and litter, foul-smelling brown water flowed out of a culvert. “We’ve got way too many challenges,” said Semadi Manganye, the chief executive of Alexandra Water Warriors, an environmental NGO that organises clean-ups of the river and plants trees on its banks. “If it’s not electricity, it’s water. If it’s not water, it’s waste.” Manganye acknowledged the challenges of providing public services in a city whose population grew by 10% to 4.8 million between the 2011 and 2022 censuses. “I have an understanding of why they’re failing,” he said.

items.title: ‘We’re doomed anyway’: young people disheartened about the future are splashing out on the present
items.summary: Spending $8 on a matcha every day seems worth it when the alternatives – like saving for a house – feel virtually unattainable An Tran treats herself to experiences like concerts and movie tickets. The 21-year-old Sydney law student, who is working towards paying her tuition…
items.body: The 21-year-old Sydney law student, who is working towards paying her tuition fees, says many of her friends spend their spare money on matcha, Labubu toys and trending makeup items. Tran, who moved from Vietnam two years ago, says she appreciates what she has in Australia but can understand why young people like her are concerned about the future. Young people feeling disheartened about the economy are choosing to spend their money in the present – regularly buying “little treats” such as takeaway coffees or even “doomspending” if it feels like there’s no point saving for the future. “If we believe in the future, we are much more likely to be able to defer gratification in the pursuit of it,” says brand strategist Eugene Healey.

items.title: On India's east coast, tidepooling inspires marine conservation
items.body: VISAKHAPATNAM, India -- On a mildly humid evening in early winter, the beach adjoining Tenneti Park in Visakhapatnam, on India's eastern seaboard, is quiet. The receding tide has exposed a broad stretch of dark rocky outcrops covered with algae and dotted with pools of seawater. A few people linger on the sand and at the water's edge, but the outcrops are deserted. The steady sound of waves fills the background.
